item.title: SF Giants to Open MLB’s 2026 Season Against New York Yankees at Oracle Park Wednesday
item.description: The SF Giants will face off with the New York Yankees on Opening Day Wednesday, and fans who aren’t attending the game at Oracle Park will need to subscribe to Netflix to watch, plus a slew of other streaming channels throughout the season.

item.title: Will There Be Bidding War for Westwood Highlands Home That Was Site of Murder-Suicide?
item.description: The home on Monterey Boulevard in SF's Westwood Highlands where investigators believe a mother killed her husband and two daughters before taking her own life last October is now up for sale.

item.title: Report: More Than 150,000 US COVID Deaths Were Unreported In 2020 and 2021
item.description: A new study found that about 16% of people who died from COVID-19 in the first two years of the pandemic weren’t counted in the official US tally, totalling about 155,000. This is on top of the 840,000 officially reported deaths, as many of these died outside of hospitals.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: Suspect at Large After Civic Center Stabbing
item.description: A person was stabbed in the Civic Center area Monday; the immigration court in SF just removed some 500 people "in absentia"; and Markwayne Mullin has been confirmed as the new DHS secretary.

item.title: Insanity Plea Entered Days Before Trial Was Set to Start In Murder of SF Tech Worker Kimberly Wong
item.description: Two and a half years after the death of 27-year-old product designer Kimberly Wong in her Presidio Heights apartment, her boyfriend Scott Fisher was set to go on trial this week for her murder. But on Monday, he changed his plea to not guilty by reason of insanity.

item.title: Tuesday Morning Topline: Voters Largely Disinterested In Governor's Race
item.description: California voters are showing a "historically high lack of awareness" of the governor's race; a planned debate between the candidates tonight was canceled; and Foster City continues to be under a ransomware attack.

item.title: SFPD May Have Violated Sanctuary Laws By Helping ICE at SFO, Bystander Files Lawsuit
item.description: A witness at SFO Sunday filed a complaint that SFPD officers violated sanctuary laws by shielding ICE agents in plainclothes from bystanders who were asking them to identify themselves, as the ICE agents attempted to restrain a woman being deported with her young daughter.

item.title: Another Technical Glitch Caused False Earthquake Alerts to Go Out In Northern California
item.description: For the second time in four months, a false-alarm alert about an earthquake was triggered in Northern California, and this was actually multiple alerts, but this time there thankfully were no loud alarms on cellphones rattling Bay Area residents awake.

item.title: French Laundry Hit With Class-Action Labor Suit Alleging Break and Wage Violations
item.description: A former dishwasher at the French Laundry in Yountville has filed a lawsuit on behalf of 50 other employees alleging that the restaurant routinely violates state law around mandatory break times and resting facilities, and that it also failed to pay the minimum wage or overtime.

item.title: Families of 2024 West Portal Crash Victims Move Forward With Civil Suits Against Mary Lau
item.description: Elderly driver Mary Lau will have to explain what happened in the 2024 West Portal crash that killed a family of four in two civil lawsuits filed by relatives of the family last year, and jurors will determine monetary damages, following Lau’s sentence in criminal court last Friday.

item.title: Florida Woman Convicted In Case of Botched Butt Injections That Killed Kim Kardashian Lookalike Model
item.description: A Florida-based cosmetologist who came to the Bay Area to administer silicone butt injections to a 34-year-old OnlyFans model in 2023 has been convicted in San Mateo County of involuntary manslaughter.

item.title: Man Killed By 38-Geary Bus Near SF's Union Square After Apparent Fall Into Street
item.description: A male pedestrian was struck and killed by a Muni bus early Tuesday morning near Union Square, after he reportedly fell from the sidewalk into the path of the bus.

item.title: Developer Bets on 'Office Resort' at Revamped Building Near Embarcadero
item.description: A building that's undergoing a significant renovation at 88 Spear Street, including a rooftop bar and restaurant, aims to be a new model for selling employees on going happily back to the office.

item.title: Police Pull Over Oakland Woman After Thieves Put License Plates Tied to Crime on Her Car
item.description: An Oakland woman discovered that her license plates had been swapped with stolen plates that were linked to a serious crime — after she was pulled over by Hayward police who were tipped off by a Flock license plate reader.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: Bill Cosby to Pay $59 Million In 1972 Sexual Assault of Sausalito Waitress
item.description: A San Jose daycare owner was convicted in the 2023 drowning of two toddlers; OpenAI pledged $1 billion in grant funding utilizing AI to advance life sciences, community programs, and other fields; and Bill Cosy was ordered to pay $59.25 million in damages to a former Sausalito waitress.
